To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the hydrocarbons in marine sediment samples from three different basins off southern California are similar in their distribution of hydrocarbon types, but the hydrocarbon content varies considerably from one sample to the next.

(a) hydrocarbons comprise 0.05-0.64% of the total organic carbon and 2.3-18.6% of the extractable carbon in the sediments examined, (b) hydrocarbons are more abundant in sediments from the shallowest basin than in sediments from deeper basins, and (c) hydrocarbons from the sediments are more complex than hydrocarbons in petroleum.

(1) the sediment in the shallow, rapidly sedimentating basins contains the highest hydrocarbon concentrations and (2) the hydrocarbon content of the sediment does not differ greatly from basin to basin or with depth in a given basin; however, the hydrocarbon content does vary randomly with depth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the composition of organic materials in sediments, and the factors that affect their composition and the composition of the hydrocarbons derived therefrom.
the composition of the organic matter and the hydrocarbon distribution in sediments and oil shales and the effects of environment on these characteristics.
the nature of the source material for petroleum, the factors that control its formation, and the nature of the changes in composition of the organic matter in sediments as a result of burial.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the organic matter in the basins is not yet in the early stages of conversion to petroleum, although it is not in the same state as that in typical oil-shales.
the organic matter in the basins off southern California is similar in many respects, but different in some respects, from the organic matter in oil-shales.
the hydrocarbon content of marine sediments varies with the nature of the environment, and that the hydrocarbons are derived from the more complex organic matter present in the sediments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hydrocarbon content of the sediments is low and does not differ greatly with depth.
the composition of the hydrocarbon fraction of organic matter in sediments is not a reliable indicator of the composition of the petroleum that may eventually be derived from these sediments.
the composition of organic materials in sediments is controlled by the nature of the original organic matter, the nature of the sedimentary environment, and the mineral matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the composition of organic material in sediments is influenced by environment, and that the composition of hydrocarbons in the early stages of formation may differ significantly from the hydrocarbons in oil fields.
the composition of organic material is influenced by environment, and that the early stages of oil formation are complex.
the hydrocarbon composition of sediments is a function of the environment and the rate of sedimentation. (Author)
